keywords.def: the general opinion people have about someone or something
having very little strong or interesting flavour
a particular style or tradition of cooking
a common but oversimplified idea about a particular group or thing
a system that limits how much of certain goods people can buy
a situation in which something is difficult to obtain because there is not enough of it
a return to popularity or importance after a period of decline

sentences.en: British food has a bit of a reputation. I’m sure that for a lot of you, the words “British food” brings to mind boiled vegetables, overcooked meat, greasy breakfasts, and meals that are, above all, rather bland.
sentences.zh: 英国食物的名声有点一言难尽。我相信对你们中的许多人来说，“英国食物”这个词会让人联想到水煮蔬菜、煮过头的肉、油腻的早餐，以及最重要的一点——相当清淡无味。

sentences.en: British cuisine is often compared unfavourably with the food of countries such as France, Italy, Spain, or Japan.
sentences.zh: 英国料理经常被拿来与法国、意大利、西班牙或日本等国的食物进行对比，而且往往处于下风。

sentences.en: There is a common idea that while other countries have sophisticated culinary traditions, Britain somehow missed out.
sentences.zh: 人们普遍认为，虽然其他国家有着精致的烹饪传统，但英国不知怎么地错过了。

sentences.en: This stereotype is not completely new. British people themselves have made jokes about their country’s food for years.
sentences.zh: 这种刻板印象并不是什么新鲜事。英国人自己多年来也一直在拿自己国家的食物开玩笑。

sentences.en: But why exactly did this reputation develop?
sentences.zh: 但这种名声究竟是怎么形成的呢？

sentences.en: And is it actually true?
sentences.zh: 这真的属实吗？

sentences.en: The first thing to understand is that British food wasn’t always considered bad.
sentences.zh: 首先需要了解的是，英国食物并非一直被认为很糟糕。

sentences.en: In fact, in the 16th century, English food was comparable, similar, to the food being eaten by ordinary people in Europe.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在16世纪，英国食物与欧洲普通人吃的东西不相上下，非常相似。

sentences.en: Britain at that time was a rural society.
sentences.zh: 那时的英国还是一个农业社会。

sentences.en: Most people lived in villages and depended on the land around them.
sentences.zh: 大多数人住在村庄里，依靠周围的土地生活。

sentences.en: For ordinary people, food was simple and seasonal.
sentences.zh: 对普通人来说，食物简单且具有季节性。

sentences.en: A common meal might be a type of vegetable stew called pottage.
sentences.zh: 常见的一餐可能是一种叫做 pottage 的蔬菜炖汤。

sentences.en: This could contain vegetables and grains and, if times were good, maybe a little bit of meat or fish.
sentences.zh: 这里面可能含有蔬菜和谷物，如果日子过得好，也许还会有一点点肉或鱼。

sentences.en: Bread was also an important staple. A staple means a basic food that people eat almost every day, and bread was a staple.
sentences.zh: 面包也是一种重要的主食。主食（staple）是指人们几乎每天都吃的基本食物，而面包就是一种主食。

sentences.en: People would also potentially have dairy products from cows and sheep, and perhaps keep chickens or other animals.
sentences.zh: 人们还可能拥有来自牛羊的乳制品，或许还会养鸡或其他动物。

sentences.en: This was not luxurious food. Hunger and starvation were actually serious risks for people across Britain, across Europe at the time.
sentences.zh: 这并不是奢侈的食物。在当时的英国和整个欧洲，饥饿和挨饿实际上是人们面临的严重风险。

sentences.en: People had to make use of almost everything available to them, including eating parts of animals that we might be less comfortable eating today.
sentences.zh: 人们必须利用几乎所有能得到的东西，包括食用一些我们今天可能觉得难以接受的动物部位。

sentences.en: This kind of food wasn’t uniquely British.
sentences.zh: 这种食物并非英国独有。

sentences.en: Peasants across Europe ate simple food based on what they could grow, raise, preserve, catch.
sentences.zh: 整个欧洲的农民都吃简单的食物，这取决于他们能种植、饲养、保存或捕获什么。

sentences.en: There was nothing unusual or inferior about the British diet.
sentences.zh: 英国人的饮食并没有什么不寻常或低人一等的地方。

sentences.en: And if we look at the other end of society, British food was actually extremely elaborate.
sentences.zh: 如果我们看看社会的另一端，英国食物实际上是非常精致复杂的。

sentences.en: The food served to wealthy people and royalty was nothing like simple pottage eaten by ordinary people.
sentences.zh: 供富人和皇室享用的食物，与普通人吃的简单炖汤完全不同。

sentences.en: Aristocratic meals contained enormous quantities of meat, elaborate dishes, sugar, and imported spices.
sentences.zh: 贵族的餐食包含大量的肉类、精致的菜肴、糖和进口香料。

sentences.en: Spices such as pepper, ginger, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, and mace were used extensively in cooking.
sentences.zh: 胡椒、生姜、肉桂、丁香、肉豆蔻和肉豆蔻皮等香料在烹饪中被广泛使用。

sentences.en: They were really expensive, so they were associated with wealth and status, but they were used generously.
sentences.zh: 它们非常昂贵，因此与财富和地位联系在一起，但人们在使用时毫不吝啬。

sentences.en: Sugar was considered such a luxury that they added it to savory dishes such as meat as well.
sentences.zh: 糖被认为是一种奢侈品，以至于他们甚至会把它加到肉类等咸味菜肴中。

sentences.en: Something more complicated, though, started to happen from the 17th century onwards.
sentences.zh: 然而，从17世纪开始，发生了一些更复杂的变化。

sentences.en: France started to become powerful, or more powerful than it was.
sentences.zh: 法国开始变得强大，或者说比以前更强大了。

sentences.en: France was becoming one of the most influential countries in Europe.
sentences.zh: 法国正成为欧洲最具影响力的国家之一。

sentences.en: And French elites, French aristocrats, used food as a way of demonstrating their sophistication, their superiority.
sentences.zh: 法国精英和法国贵族将食物作为展示其精致和优越感的一种方式。

sentences.en: Cooking became more refined in France. Chefs began developing new techniques.
sentences.zh: 法国的烹饪变得更加精细。厨师们开始开发新的技术。

sentences.en: Chefs in France were creating new ways to prepare vegetables, and they started to establish rules for what was considered good food.
sentences.zh: 法国的厨师们正在创造准备蔬菜的新方法，并开始为什么是好食物制定规则。

sentences.en: And of course, British aristocrats copied them.
sentences.zh: 当然，英国贵族也效仿了他们。

sentences.en: King Charles II, for example, before he was the king, spent time in exile in France during the English Civil War.
sentences.zh: 例如，King Charles II在成为国王之前，曾在英国国会战争期间流亡法国。

sentences.en: He returned from France with an appreciation for French food and French culture.
sentences.zh: 他从法国归来时，对法国食物和法国文化十分欣赏。

sentences.en: French cuisine became really fashionable in Britain, among the wealthy classes anyway.
sentences.zh: 法国料理在英国变得非常流行，至少在富裕阶层中是这样。

sentences.en: But the food of ordinary people continued to be based on local ingredients and traditional recipes By the 18th century, some British writers were already complaining about this trend, criticizing wealthy British people who preferred French cooks to English ones.
sentences.zh: 但普通人的食物仍然以当地食材和传统食谱为主。到了18世纪，一些英国作家已经开始抱怨这种趋势，批评那些比起英国厨师更偏爱法国厨师的英国富人。

sentences.en: And there was an even bigger change happening for normal people, a change that would have a much larger effect on British cuisine.
sentences.zh: 而对于普通人来说，正在发生一个更大的变化，这个变化将对英国料理产生深远得多的影响。

sentences.en: For centuries, many rural communities had access to common land, right?
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，许多农村社区都可以使用公有地，对吧？

sentences.en: This is land that was shared among all people.
sentences.zh: 这是所有人共享的土地。

sentences.en: People could use this land for animals or to grow food or to collect resources such as firewood.
sentences.zh: 人们可以使用这片土地放牧、种植食物或收集木柴等资源。

sentences.en: But during the 18th and 19th centuries, something called “enclosure” happened.
sentences.zh: 但在18和19世纪，发生了一件被称为“圈地运动”的事情。

sentences.en: Landowners enclosed common land. Fences and boundaries were built around the land.
sentences.zh: 地主们圈占了公有地。土地周围建起了围栏和边界。

sentences.en: The land that had been previously available for people to grow their food now became privately controlled.
sentences.zh: 以前可供人们种植食物的土地，现在变成了私人控制。

sentences.en: If you lose access to the land where you keep your cows and grow your vegetables, you lose the system that allows you to feed yourself.
sentences.zh: 如果你失去了放牛和种菜的土地，你就失去了自给自足的系统。

sentences.en: It’s something that didn’t happen to France or Italy or Spain, at least not to the same extent.
sentences.zh: 这种情况在法国、意大利或西班牙并没有发生，至少没有达到同样的程度。

sentences.en: And then came an even bigger change: the Industrial Revolution.
sentences.zh: 紧接着迎来了一个更大的变化：工业革命。

sentences.en: The Industrial Revolution changed Britain from an agricultural society into an urban, industrial society.
sentences.zh: 工业革命将英国从一个农业社会转变为一个城市化的工业社会。

sentences.en: Between 1750 and 1850, millions of people moved into towns and cities to work in factories.
sentences.zh: 在1750年到1850年之间，数以百万计的人涌入城镇，在工厂工作。

sentences.en: People moved from their villages and farms into places like Manchester, Birmingham, Liverpool, and London.
sentences.zh: 人们从村庄和农场搬到了曼彻斯特、伯明翰、利物浦和伦敦等地。

sentences.en: Instead of living close to farmland and producing their own food or buying local food from their neighbors, people needed to depend on shops and markets for their meals.
sentences.zh: 人们不再住在农田附近、自己生产食物或从邻居那里购买当地食物，而是需要依靠商店和市场来解决温饱。

sentences.en: Factory work involved long hours of physically demanding labor.
sentences.zh: 工厂工作涉及长时间的高强度体力劳动。

sentences.en: If you’re in a factory, you are inside all day from 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM at night.
sentences.zh: 如果你在工厂工作，你整天都要待在里面，从早上7点一直到晚上7点。

sentences.en: Working-class families now had less time to prepare food.
sentences.zh: 工人阶级家庭现在准备食物的时间变少了。

sentences.en: They also had less money or no money of which to buy food with.
sentences.zh: 他们买食物的钱也变少了，甚至根本没有钱。

sentences.en: Meals that families ate then needed to be affordable, they needed to be really filling, and they needed to be easy to prepare.
sentences.zh: 因此，家庭食用的餐食需要价格便宜、能吃饱，而且要易于准备。

sentences.en: Bread, potatoes, oats, meat, cheese, these kinds of things became important.
sentences.zh: 面包、土豆、燕麦、肉类、奶酪这些东西变得重要起来。

sentences.en: Pies and stews, puddings, and dishes that could feed an entire family.
sentences.zh: 馅饼、炖菜、布丁，以及能喂饱全家人的菜肴。

sentences.en: This is what people started to eat. The Industrial Revolution also changed the way food was produced.
sentences.zh: 这就是人们开始吃的东西。工业革命也改变了食物的生产方式。

sentences.en: Britain became the pioneer of mass production, and this was applied to food as well.
sentences.zh: 英国成为了大规模生产的先驱，这也应用到了食品领域。

sentences.en: Factories could produce food in large quantities.
sentences.zh: 工厂可以大量生产食物。

sentences.en: Railways made it possible to move ingredients around the country.
sentences.zh: 铁路使得在全国范围内运输食材成为可能。

sentences.en: This was a big improvement in some respects.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，这是一个巨大的进步。

sentences.en: It made certain foods cheaper. Certain foods were now available more widely.
sentences.zh: 它使某些食物变得更便宜。某些食物现在的供应范围更广了。

sentences.en: People in cities could get food from other parts of the country.
sentences.zh: 城市里的人可以获得来自全国其他地方的食物。

sentences.en: But there were big downsides. People no longer knew necessarily where their ingredients came from.
sentences.zh: 但也有很大的弊端。人们不再一定知道他们的食材来自哪里。

sentences.en: A person living in an industrial city would be eating food that had traveled hundreds of kilometers and had been processed by people they never met.
sentences.zh: 一个生活在工业城市的人，吃到的食物可能已经运输了数百公里，并且是由他们从未见过的人加工的。

sentences.en: And because working-class people had limited incomes, the quality of the food was not the priority.
sentences.zh: 而且由于工人阶级的收入有限，食物的质量并不是首要考虑的。

sentences.en: They needed food that would provide them with enough energy to get through a difficult working day.
sentences.zh: 他们需要能提供足够能量的食物，来度过艰难的工作日。

sentences.en: Britain was the first country to have this massive urbanization.
sentences.zh: 英国是第一个经历如此大规模城市化的国家。

sentences.en: A country is considered to be an agricultural society until about less than 50% of the workforce is no longer in agricultural work.
sentences.zh: 一个国家在农业劳动力比例降至约50%以下之前，都被视为农业社会。

sentences.en: Britain stopped being an agricultural society in the early 1800s, and the transition away from being an agricultural society started about 50 years before that, in the 1750s.
sentences.zh: 英国在19世纪初就不再是农业社会了，而脱离农业社会的转型早在约50年前的1750年代就已经开始。

sentences.en: So people in Britain have lived far away from their food and ingredients for quite a long time.
sentences.zh: 因此，英国人远离食物和食材源头的生活已经持续了相当长的时间。

sentences.en: But compare that to places with great food cultures.
sentences.zh: 但相比之下，那些拥有优秀饮食文化的地方就不同了。

sentences.en: France only reached the level of not being an agricultural society in the 1930s, Italy in the 1950s, Spain in the 1950s as well, Japan in the 1920s, China in the 2000s.
sentences.zh: 法国直到1930年代才达到不再是农业社会的水平，意大利在1950年代，西班牙也在1950年代，日本在1920年代，中国则在2000年代。

sentences.en: Countries like this with great food cultures partly have a great food culture because people were around their food for much longer and much more recently.
sentences.zh: 这些拥有优秀饮食文化的国家，部分原因在于人们与食物接触的时间要长得多，而且这种紧密联系在更近的历史中依然存在。

sentences.en: If the Industrial Revolution changed the way British people produced and ate food, the World Wars changed what people could eat.
sentences.zh: 如果说工业革命改变了英国人生产和食用食物的方式，那么两次世界大战则改变了人们能吃到的东西。

sentences.en: During the First World War, Britain experienced real food shortages.
sentences.zh: 第一次世界大战期间，英国经历了真正的食物短缺。

sentences.en: Britain depended on imported food at the time, but German submarines threatened all the ships crossing the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 英国当时依赖进口食物，但德国潜艇威胁着所有横跨大西洋的船只。

sentences.en: So the British government encouraged people to grow their own vegetables.
sentences.zh: 因此，英国政府鼓励人们自己种植蔬菜。

sentences.en: During the Second World War, in January 1940, Britain introduced food rationing.
sentences.zh: 第二次世界大战期间，在1940年1月，英国实行了食物配给制。

sentences.en: Food rationing means limiting the foods available.
sentences.zh: 食物配给意味着限制可获得的食物。

sentences.en: People were told what they could eat. They were given a ration book, which gave them coupons to exchange for certain ingredients.
sentences.zh: 人们被告知可以吃什么。他们拿到了一本配给书，里面有可以用来兑换特定食材的票券。

sentences.en: And they could only purchase certain quantities of particular foods.
sentences.zh: 而且他们只能购买特定数量的特定食物。

sentences.en: Items like meat, butter, bacon, sugar, eggs, and cheese were restricted.
sentences.zh: 肉类、黄油、培根、糖、鸡蛋和奶酪等物品都受到了限制。

sentences.en: Some foods were completely unavailable. This produced a very unusual food culture.
sentences.zh: 有些食物完全买不到。这产生了一种非常奇特的饮食文化。

sentences.en: People were encouraged to use cheap ingredients and substitute ingredients when it was too difficult to find the correct thing.
sentences.zh: 在很难找到合适食材的时候，人们被鼓励使用廉价食材和替代品。

sentences.en: When you don’t have much meat, butter, eggs, sugar, you don’t really have opportunities to create tasty dishes.
sentences.zh: 当你没有多少肉、黄油、鸡蛋和糖时，你真的没有机会做出美味的菜肴。

sentences.en: And when the country is at war, making nice food is not really the priority of most people.
sentences.zh: 而且当国家处于战争状态时，做出美味的食物并不是大多数人的首要任务。

sentences.en: Rationing, though, did not mean that British food became universally terrible.
sentences.zh: 不过，配给制并不意味着英国食物变得一无是处。

sentences.en: People still had vegetables, fish and bread and potatoes and other ingredients.
sentences.zh: 人们仍然有蔬菜、鱼、面包、土豆和其他食材。

sentences.en: People learned how to make nutritious meals from their supplies.
sentences.zh: 人们学会了如何用手头的供应做出营养丰富的餐食。

sentences.en: Some wartime dishes are still around today and they’re examples of British food culture.
sentences.zh: 一些战争时期的菜肴至今仍然存在，它们是英国饮食文化的代表。

sentences.en: The bigger problem, though, is that food rationing in Britain didn’t end until 1954, almost nine years after the Second World War had finished.
sentences.zh: 然而，更大的问题是，英国的食物配给直到1954年才结束，这几乎是在第二次世界大战结束九年之后。

sentences.en: This was later than France ended their rationing, and actually even later than Germany.
sentences.zh: 这比法国结束配给的时间还要晚，实际上甚至比德国还要晚。

sentences.en: What this means is that an entire generation of British people grew up in a society that had experienced food scarcity and limited food choices.
sentences.zh: 这意味着整整一代英国人是在一个经历过食物匮乏和食物选择有限的社会中长大的。

sentences.en: A lot of food culture is about habits and expectations.
sentences.zh: 许多饮食文化都与习惯和期望有关。

sentences.en: If you go to a country like Italy, people tend to learn how to cook delicious food from their grandparents.
sentences.zh: 如果你去像意大利这样的国家，人们往往会向祖父母学习如何烹饪美味的食物。

sentences.en: But if your grandparents learned to cook during food rationing, your parents would have grown up eating simple meals, and those habits continue and get transferred down society.
sentences.zh: 但如果你的祖父母是在食物配给期间学会做饭的，你的父母就会在吃简单饭菜的环境中长大，这些习惯就会延续并代代相传。

sentences.en: When people imagine traditional British food, they picture boiled vegetables with potatoes and gravy and mild flavors.
sentences.zh: 当人们想象传统的英国食物时，脑海中浮现的是水煮蔬菜配土豆、肉汁和清淡的味道。

sentences.en: This was the result of World War II. There were no spices.
sentences.zh: 这就是第二次世界大战的结果。当时没有香料。

sentences.en: Ingredients were really scarce. People did make delicious food, but perhaps it’s not the food that you’d consider tasty in the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 食材非常匮乏。人们确实做出了美味的食物，但也许那并不是你在21世纪会觉得好吃的食物。

sentences.en: And this is actually partly where the stereotype of British food becoming bad comes from.
sentences.zh: 这实际上也是英国食物“难吃”这一刻板印象的部分来源。

sentences.en: It’s often traced to soldiers from the USA arriving in Britain after World War II and discovering the food was not tasty, the food was poor quality.
sentences.zh: 这通常可以追溯到二战后抵达英国的美国士兵，他们发现这里的食物不好吃，而且质量很差。

sentences.en: By 1954, Britain ended food rationing, but that did not mean that British food returned to great traditional cooking.
sentences.zh: 到了1954年，英国结束了食物配给，但这并不意味着英国食物恢复了优秀的传统烹饪。

sentences.en: People in Britain were becoming wealthier and even more urban than they had been before.
sentences.zh: 英国人变得比以前更富裕，城市化程度也更高了。

sentences.en: Women started to enter employment in greater numbers.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的女性开始步入职场。

sentences.en: Technology that was used in houses was changing.
sentences.zh: 家中使用的技术也在发生变化。

sentences.en: Supermarkets started to spread to every town.
sentences.zh: 超市开始普及到每个城镇。

sentences.en: For the first time, many British families had access to a wide range of food.
sentences.zh: 许多英国家庭第一次能够接触到种类繁多的食物。

sentences.en: But that did not produce better cooking.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有带来更好的烹饪。

sentences.en: More choice does not really lead to better cooking.
sentences.zh: 更多的选择并不一定会带来更好的烹饪。

sentences.en: The post-war decades saw the growth of processed food and convenience food: frozen vegetables, canned food, instant meals, microwave meals.
sentences.zh: 战后的几十年见证了加工食品和便利食品的增长：冷冻蔬菜、罐头食品、即食食品、微波炉加热食品。

sentences.en: This wasn’t uniquely British, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并非英国独有。

sentences.en: Similar things have happened in every country.
sentences.zh: 每个国家都发生过类似的事情。

sentences.en: Some traditional cooking practices and skills began to be forgotten.
sentences.zh: 一些传统的烹饪习惯和技巧开始被遗忘。

sentences.en: For example, vegetables were boiled much longer than necessary because people just didn’t know how to cook.
sentences.zh: 例如，蔬菜被煮得比需要的时间长得多，因为人们根本不知道怎么做饭。

sentences.en: Meat was cooked until it was extremely well done, partly due to misunderstandings about food safety.
sentences.zh: 肉被煮到熟透甚至变老，部分原因是对食品安全的误解。

sentences.en: Ready-made sauces and frozen foods became common.
sentences.zh: 现成的酱料和冷冻食品变得很常见。

sentences.en: They were easier than making your own sauce.
sentences.zh: 它们比自己调制酱汁要容易得多。

sentences.en: And people’s school food had a particularly poor reputation.
sentences.zh: 此外，学校的伙食名声尤其糟糕。

sentences.en: Countries such as France and Italy have really developed reputations as great sophisticated cuisines.
sentences.zh: 法国和意大利等国确实树立了精致美味料理的声誉。

sentences.en: British cuisine, though, is associated with pubs and fish and chips and fried breakfasts.
sentences.zh: 然而，英国料理却让人联想到酒吧、炸鱼薯条和煎炸早餐。

sentences.en: At exactly the same time, though, Britain was also becoming an incredibly multicultural society.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，英国也正在成为一个极其多元文化的社会。

sentences.en: Large numbers of people arrived from South Asia and the Caribbean and Africa after the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 第二次世界大战后，大量人口从南亚、加勒比地区和非洲来到英国。

sentences.en: They brought their own food traditions with them, and these foods have gradually become part of British life.
sentences.zh: 他们带来了自己的饮食传统，这些食物逐渐成为英国生活的一部分。

sentences.en: There are Indian restaurants across British cities.
sentences.zh: 英国各地的城市里都有印度餐厅。

sentences.en: Chinese takeaways in every town. Caribbean food is quite visible, especially in places like London.
sentences.zh: 每个城镇都有中餐外卖。加勒比食物也很常见，尤其是在伦敦等地。

sentences.en: You can also find cuisines from the Middle East, East Asia, and many other parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 你还可以找到来自中东、东亚和世界许多其他地方的美食。

sentences.en: One of the most common criticisms of British food is that it is bland.
sentences.zh: 对英国食物最常见的批评之一是它清淡无味。

sentences.en: When people say this, they basically mean that British food doesn’t really use spices.
sentences.zh: 当人们这么说时，基本上是指英国食物不怎么使用香料。

sentences.en: There is a common joke on the internet that Britain colonized the world for spices, but never really used them.
sentences.zh: 网上有一个流传很广的笑话，说英国为了香料殖民了世界，却从未真正使用过它们。

sentences.en: This isn’t really true. British cooking historically used loads of spices: black pepper, ginger, nutmeg, cinnamon, cloves, mustard, and mace.
sentences.zh: 这并不完全属实。英国烹饪在历史上使用了大量的香料：黑胡椒、生姜、肉豆蔻、肉桂、丁香、芥末和肉豆蔻皮。

sentences.en: Spices appear in traditional British recipes for meat, desserts, sauces, baked goods, and drinks.
sentences.zh: 香料出现在传统的英国肉类、甜点、酱汁、烘焙食品和饮料的食谱中。

sentences.en: Black pudding is a traditional spiced blood sausage and part of a traditional breakfast.
sentences.zh: 黑布丁（Black pudding）是一种传统的调味血肠，也是传统早餐的一部分。

sentences.en: British Christmas food, like mince pies, are full of spices like nutmeg, cinnamon, mace.
sentences.zh: 英国的圣诞食物，比如圣诞肉馅饼（mince pies），充满了肉豆蔻、肉桂、肉豆蔻皮等香料。

sentences.en: You’ll find spices especially in British desserts.
sentences.zh: 你会发现香料在英国甜点中尤为常见。

sentences.en: But for much of history, spices were really expensive.
sentences.zh: 但在历史上的大部分时间里，香料都非常昂贵。

sentences.en: They traveled a long way to get to the UK.
sentences.zh: 它们要经过长途跋涉才能到达英国。

sentences.en: The UK grows lots of delicious herbs, mint and rosemary and thyme, we use a lot of that in our cooking.
sentences.zh: 英国种植了许多美味的草本植物，如薄荷、迷迭香和百里香，我们在烹饪中经常使用它们。

sentences.en: But spices were expensive. They were grown on the other side of the world.
sentences.zh: 但香料很贵。它们是在世界的另一端种植的。

sentences.en: British cuisine didn’t develop around the idea of intense spicing.
sentences.zh: 英国料理的发展并不是围绕着浓重香料的概念展开的。

sentences.en: This is something you find in South Asia, in the Middle East, and Southeast Asia.
sentences.zh: 这是你在南亚、中东和东南亚才能发现的特点。

sentences.en: Food culture there relies on using lots of intense flavors and spices.
sentences.zh: 那里的饮食文化依赖于使用大量浓烈的风味和香料。

sentences.en: Traditional British cooking relied on the flavor of the main ingredients.
sentences.zh: 传统的英国烹饪依赖于主要食材本身的风味。

sentences.en: A roast joint of beef would usually just be seasoned with salt and pepper, some herbs as well, and then served with vegetables and gravy and perhaps horseradish or mustard.
sentences.zh: 一大块烤牛肉通常只用盐、胡椒和一些草药调味，然后搭配蔬菜、肉汁，或许还有辣根或芥末一起食用。

sentences.en: Perhaps the best challenge to the idea that British food is bland is found in “curry”.
sentences.zh: 也许对“英国食物清淡无味”这一观点最好的反驳，就存在于“咖喱”之中。

sentences.en: Walk through any British town or city and you will find Indian restaurants.
sentences.zh: 走在任何一个英国城镇或城市的街头，你都会发现印度餐厅。

sentences.en: I grew up in a town of less than 5,000 people, and that town had four Indian restaurants.
sentences.zh: 我在一个人口不足5000人的小镇长大，而那个小镇就有四家印度餐厅。

sentences.en: Curry has become such a normal part of British life.
sentences.zh: 咖喱已经成为英国生活里非常普通的一部分。

sentences.en: There is an obvious difference between food from India and food that was created in Britain by people of South Asian heritage.
sentences.zh: 印度本土的食物与南亚裔移民在英国创造的食物之间有着明显的区别。

sentences.en: Britain has a large South Asian population, and British Indian cuisine developed through the mix of South Asian cooking traditions and British ingredients and tastes.
sentences.zh: 英国有大量的南亚裔人口，英式印度料理是通过南亚烹饪传统与英国食材及口味的融合而发展起来的。

sentences.en: Chicken tikka masala is perhaps the most famous example.
sentences.zh: 提卡烤鸡玛萨拉（Chicken tikka masala）也许是最著名的例子。

sentences.en: This is, for a long time, considered the national dish of the UK.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，这被认为是英国的国菜。

sentences.en: Its exact origins are disputed, but it’s generally understood to be a product of the British Indian restaurant tradition.
sentences.zh: 它的确切起源尚存争议，但人们普遍认为它是英式印度餐厅传统的产物。

sentences.en: It uses the language and the techniques of Indian cuisine, but was adapted for British flavors.
sentences.zh: 它使用了印度料理的语言和技术，但为了适应英国人的口味进行了改良。

sentences.en: And chicken tikka masala isn’t alone. The chicken balti, for example, was invented in Birmingham in the 1970s by Pakistani immigrants and is now a major part of Birmingham’s food culture.
sentences.zh: 提卡烤鸡玛萨拉并非个例。例如，巴尔蒂鸡肉（chicken balti）是1970年代由巴基斯坦移民在伯明翰发明的，现在是伯明翰饮食文化的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: If you go to Birmingham, you’ll see hundreds, maybe even thousands of restaurants selling baltis.
sentences.zh: 如果你去伯明翰，你会看到成百上千家销售巴尔蒂的餐厅。

sentences.en: British curry houses develop their own styles of curries and their own sauces and breads that aren’t really found in South Asia.
sentences.zh: 英国的咖喱屋开发出了自己独特风格的咖喱、酱汁和烤饼，这些在南亚是找不到的。

sentences.en: The foods might have South Asian roots and inspiration, but they are uniquely found in Britain.
sentences.zh: 这些食物可能源于南亚并受到其启发，但它们是英国独有的。

sentences.en: This isn’t unusual. Most countries around the world have incorporated foods introduced by immigrants.
sentences.zh: 这并不罕见。世界上大多数国家都融入了由移民引入的食物。

sentences.en: Take the United States. Pizza is very strongly associated with New York food culture, even though pizza is an Italian food, originated in Italy.
sentences.zh: 以美国为例。披萨与纽约的饮食文化有着极强的联系，尽管披萨是一种源自意大利的意大利食物。

sentences.en: Italian immigrants moved to the US, transformed the dish pizza to a new style, created New York and Chicago pizzas that are now distinctly American.
sentences.zh: 意大利移民移居美国，将披萨这道菜转变为一种新的风格，创造了现在具有鲜明美国特色的纽约披萨和芝加哥披萨。

sentences.en: Consider Germany, where the doner kebab is an enormously popular fast food.
sentences.zh: 再看看德国，旋转烤肉（doner kebab）是一种极受欢迎的快餐。

sentences.en: Doner was developed in Germany by Turkish immigrants.
sentences.zh: 旋转烤肉是由土耳其移民在德国开发出来的。

sentences.en: There are so many more examples. Chinese immigrants, in particular, transformed the food of Southeast Asia.
sentences.zh: 还有很多这样的例子。尤其是中国移民，改变了东南亚的食物。

sentences.en: If you go to Singapore or Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, the Philippines, you will find dishes that are inspired by Chinese cuisine, but they are now considered dishes of those countries.
sentences.zh: 如果你去新加坡、马来西亚、印度尼西亚、泰国或菲律宾，你会发现受到中餐启发的菜肴，但它们现在已被视为这些国家的代表性菜肴。

sentences.en: Perhaps the best example I can think of, one that’s relevant to where I live now, is the famous Japanese noodle dish “ramen “.
sentences.zh: 我能想到的最好的例子，也是与我目前居住的地方相关的一个例子，就是著名的日本面食“拉面”（ramen）。

sentences.en: Ramen was introduced by Chinese immigrants and can trace its history to Yokohama’s Chinatown in the late 1800s.
sentences.zh: 拉面是由中国移民引入的，其历史可以追溯到19世纪末横滨的唐人街。

sentences.en: The first ramen-only restaurants only opened in Japan in the 1920s, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想，日本第一家专门的拉面馆直到1920年代才开业。

sentences.en: The first curry house in the UK, opened in 1810… 100 years earlier.
sentences.zh: 而英国的第一家咖喱屋开业于1810年……整整早了100年。

sentences.en: If ramen is considered a Japanese food, surely curry can be considered a British food, or at least a British Indian food.
sentences.zh: 如果拉面被认为是一种日本食物，那么咖喱当然也可以被认为是一种英国食物，或者至少是英式印度食物。

sentences.en: Britain’s most famous dish is fish and chips.
sentences.zh: 英国最著名的菜肴是炸鱼薯条。

sentences.en: Fried fish has connections to Jewish communities who came to Britain from Spain and Portugal.
sentences.zh: 炸鱼与从西班牙和葡萄牙来到英国的犹太人社区有关。

sentences.en: Potatoes originated in South America. But nobody seriously argues that fish and chips isn’t British.
sentences.zh: 土豆起源于南美洲。但没有人会认真争论炸鱼薯条不是英国菜。

sentences.en: We accept that they are British because of their history.
sentences.zh: 我们因为它们的历史而接受它们是英国的。

sentences.en: Indian food is Indian, of course. But British Indian food can also be British.
sentences.zh: 印度食物当然是印度的。但英式印度食物也可以是英国的。

sentences.en: It was created through migration and has become part of British food culture.
sentences.zh: 它是通过移民创造的，并已成为英国饮食文化的一部分。

sentences.en: If you only look at the dishes that existed in Britain in the 1940s, you’re gonna miss a huge part of what British people actually eat.
sentences.zh: 如果你只看1940年代存在于英国的菜肴，你将会错过英国人实际吃的东西的很大一部分。

sentences.en: The stereotype of British food being bad hasn’t disappeared, but Britain has a much more sophisticated and diverse food culture now.
sentences.zh: 英国食物难吃的刻板印象并未消失，但英国现在拥有更加精致和多元的饮食文化。

sentences.en: British chefs have taken traditional foods and prepare them in new ways.
sentences.zh: 英国厨师们采用了传统食材，并用新的方式来准备它们。

sentences.en: Some people describe it as a revival of British cuisine.
sentences.zh: 有些人将其描述为英国料理的复兴。

sentences.en: There are some genuinely excellent ingredients available in Britain.
sentences.zh: 英国有一些真正优秀的食材。

sentences.en: British cheeses are a good example. Cheddar is probably the most internationally famous British cheese, but Britain has hundreds of cheeses: Stilton, Red Leicester, Wensleydale, Lancashire, and lots more.
sentences.zh: 英国奶酪就是一个很好的例子。切达奶酪（Cheddar）可能是国际上最著名的英国奶酪，但英国有数百种奶酪：斯蒂尔顿（Stilton）、红莱斯特（Red Leicester）、温斯利代尔（Wensleydale）、兰开夏（Lancashire）等等。

sentences.en: Britain also has excellent seafood. There’s also great meat in the UK, a lot of free-range animals.
sentences.zh: 英国也有极好的海鲜。英国还有很棒的肉类，有很多放养的动物。

sentences.en: There is a strong tradition of British baking.
sentences.zh: 英国烘焙有着深厚的传统。

sentences.en: Cakes, biscuits, pies, tarts, puddings. These are things that I like.
sentences.zh: 蛋糕、饼干、馅饼、挞、布丁。这些都是我喜欢的东西。

sentences.en: A well-made sticky toffee pudding is perhaps the best dessert in the world, in my opinion.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，制作精良的太妃糖布丁（sticky toffee pudding）也许是世界上最好的甜点。

sentences.en: Another important development in British food recently has been the transformation of the pub.
sentences.zh: 最近英国食物的另一个重要发展是酒吧的转型。

sentences.en: The traditional British pub was a place to drink, but now modern pubs have become restaurants as well.
sentences.zh: 传统的英国酒吧是一个喝酒的地方，但现在的现代酒吧也变成了餐厅。

sentences.en: British chefs have also become really internationally respected.
sentences.zh: 英国厨师在国际上也变得非常受人尊敬。

sentences.en: Chefs such as Gordon Ramsay, Heston Blumenthal have changed the perception of British cooking.
sentences.zh: 像 Gordon Ramsay、Heston Blumenthal 这样的厨师改变了人们对英国烹饪的看法。

sentences.en: The UK has a lot of Michelin-starred restaurants.
sentences.zh: 英国有很多米其林星级餐厅。

sentences.en: And most of the Michelin-starred restaurants in the UK cook British food or modern British food.
sentences.zh: 英国的大多数米其林星级餐厅烹饪的都是英国食物或现代英国食物。

sentences.en: And there are so many other restaurants that are not Michelin-starred selling great British dishes and great British food.
sentences.zh: 还有很多其他非米其林星级的餐厅在销售极好的英国菜肴 and 极好的英国食物。

sentences.en: I’ve had people tell me before that they’ve been to London and they’ve not found anything nice to eat in London, which is incredible’cause London is perhaps one of the best food cities in the entire world.
sentences.zh: 以前有人告诉我，他们去过伦敦，但在伦敦没找到什么好吃的东西，这真是令人难以置信，因为伦敦也许是整个世界上最好的美食城市之一。

sentences.en: There is so much delicious food, great restaurants in London.
sentences.zh: 伦敦有那么多美味的食物和棒极了的餐厅。

sentences.en: Part of it might be a financial problem.
sentences.zh: 部分原因可能是经济问题。

sentences.en: Restaurants in the UK are quite expensive.
sentences.zh: 英国的餐厅相当昂贵。

sentences.en: People in the UK do not eat out for every meal.
sentences.zh: 英国人并不会每顿饭都在外面吃。

sentences.en: Usually, eating out at a restaurant might be something a family does once or twice a month maybe less, maybe more, but it’s not something completely regular.
sentences.zh: 通常，去餐厅吃饭可能是家庭一个月一两次的活动，也许更少，也许更多，但并不是完全常规的事情。

sentences.en: The issue is that people often go to chain restaurants or places that are known for selling cheap, mass-produced food.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，人们经常去连锁餐厅或以销售廉价、大规模生产的食物而闻名的地方。

sentences.en: If you go to the USA and just eat McDonald’s, are you going to think the food in the US is great?
sentences.zh: 如果你去了美国只吃麦当劳，你会觉得美国的食物很棒吗？

sentences.en: Probably not. So if you are visiting Britain, what should you actually eat?
sentences.zh: 大概不会。所以如果你去英国旅游，你到底应该吃什么？

sentences.en: The most obvious choice is fish and chips: fried fish, usually cod or haddock, with thick-cut chips served with salt and vinegar.
sentences.zh: 最显而易见的选择是炸鱼薯条：炸鱼（通常是鳕鱼或黑线鳕），搭配粗切薯条，撒上盐和醋。

sentences.en: Probably Britain’s most internationally famous dish.
sentences.zh: 这可能是英国在国际上最著名的菜肴。

sentences.en: Another classic meal is the Sunday roast.
sentences.zh: 另一道经典餐食是周日烤肉（Sunday roast）。

sentences.en: Traditionally, this is eaten on Sundays, hence the name, and it involves roasted meat, chicken, pork, lamb, beef, sometimes other things like turkey as well potatoes, vegetables, gravy, Yorkshire pudding.
sentences.zh: 传统上，这道菜在周日食用，因此得名，它包括烤肉（鸡肉、猪肉、羊肉、牛肉，有时也有火鸡等其他肉类）、土豆、蔬菜、肉汁和约克郡布丁。

sentences.en: It’s incredibly delicious, and I’d recommend going to a nice pub and ordering a nice Sunday roast if you can.
sentences.zh: 它非常美味，我建议如果可以的话，去一家不错的酒吧点一份美味的周日烤肉。

sentences.en: For breakfast, you can try full English breakfasts: eggs, bacon, sausages, beans, mushrooms, tomatoes, and toast, sometimes black pudding as well.
sentences.zh: 早餐方面，你可以尝试英式全套早餐：鸡蛋、培根、香肠、茄汁豆、蘑菇、西红柿和吐司，有时还有黑布丁。

sentences.en: British cuisine is also particularly good at pies and pastries.
sentences.zh: 英国料理也特别擅长制作馅饼和糕点。

sentences.en: A steak and ale pie or a shepherd’s pie or a Cornish pasty are great.
sentences.zh: 麦芽酒牛肉派（steak and ale pie）、牧羊人派（shepherd’s pie）或康沃尔肉馅饼（Cornish pasty）都很棒。

sentences.en: British food also has lots of desserts and cakes: sticky toffee pudding, Eton mess, bread and butter pudding.
sentences.zh: 英国食物也有许多甜点 and 蛋糕：太妃糖布丁、伊顿麦斯（Eton mess）、面包黄油布丁。

sentences.en: They’re all worth trying. There’s also regional food in the UK as well.
sentences.zh: 它们都值得一试。英国也有地方特色食物。

sentences.en: Cornwall has Cornish pasties. Lancashire has Lancashire hotpot.
sentences.zh: 康沃尔有康沃尔肉馅饼。兰开夏有兰开夏大锅炖（Lancashire hotpot）。

sentences.en: Wales has Welsh rarebit. Scotland has so many dishes: haggis and Cullen skink.
sentences.zh: 威尔士有威尔士干酪吐司（Welsh rarebit）。苏格兰有非常多的菜肴：哈吉斯（haggis）和库伦鱼汤（Cullen skink）。

sentences.en: And there is the food that represents modern Britain.
sentences.zh: 还有代表现代英国的食物。

sentences.en: You should absolutely try a British Indian curry.
sentences.zh: 你绝对应该尝试一下英式印度咖喱。

sentences.en: And if you want to see the modern British food revival, go to a great gastropub or a contemporary British restaurant.
sentences.zh: 如果你想见识现代英国食物的复兴，可以去一家棒极了的美食酒吧（gastropub）或现代英国餐厅。

sentences.en: Don’t just go to the supermarket and buy a sandwich and complain that British food is bad.
sentences.zh: 不要只是去超市买个三明治，然后抱怨英国食物难吃。

sentences.en: Go and buy nice food, and then see if it’s actually tasty.
sentences.zh: 去买点好吃的，然后看看它是不是真的很美味。

sentences.en: When I studied in London, I had two friends from France and Spain who used to complain about British food all the time.
sentences.zh: 我在伦敦读书时，有两个来自法国和西班牙的朋友，他们过去总是抱怨英国食物。

sentences.en: It turns out they never really tried British food.
sentences.zh: 结果发现他们从未真正尝试过英国食物。

sentences.en: They just complained about it. I took them to a farmers market that popped up near the university every Wednesday, and I bought them some pies.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在抱怨。我带他们去了每周三在大学附近举办的农贸市场，给他们买了一些馅饼。

sentences.en: They would go back to that market every week or almost every week to buy the same pies because they thought they were so tasty.
sentences.zh: 之后他们每周或几乎每周都会回到那个市场买同样的馅饼，因为他们觉得太好吃了。

sentences.en: The reality is that perhaps British food is not the best cuisine in the world.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，也许英国食物并不是世界上最好的料理。

sentences.en: There are lots of countries around the world that make delicious food.
sentences.zh: 世界上有很多国家都能做出美味的食物。

sentences.en: But Britain doesn’t necessarily deserve its negative reputation.
sentences.zh: 但英国不应该承受这样的负面名声。

sentences.en: Perhaps British food isn’t quite as bad as you think.
sentences.zh: 也许英国食物并没有你想象的那么糟。

sentences.en: Its reputation has a complicated history.
sentences.zh: 它的名声有着复杂的历史背景。

sentences.en: It’s related to industrialization, war, rationing, social changes, and Britain’s relationship with the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 这与工业化、战争、配给制、社会变革以及英国与世界其他地区的关系有关。

sentences.en: Food changes and evolves. Every country’s food changes.
sentences.zh: 食物在改变和演变。每个国家的食物都在发生变化。

sentences.en: Even where you live, your country, your food culture, is going to have terrible dishes.
sentences.zh: 即使在你居住的地方，你国家的饮食文化中也会有一些糟糕的菜肴。

sentences.en: Every country does. It’s also gonna have great dishes.
sentences.zh: 每个国家都是如此。但同样也会有极好的菜肴。

sentences.en: If you go to Britain, you can eat great food, you can eat terrible food.
sentences.zh: 如果你去了英国，你既能吃到极好的食物，也能吃到糟糕的食物。

sentences.en: But what do you think? Does British food deserve its bad reputation?
sentences.zh: 但你是怎么想的呢？英国食物配得上它的坏名声吗？

sentences.en: If you’ve ever tried British food, did something surprise you?
sentences.zh: 如果你曾尝试过英国食物，有什么让你感到惊讶的吗？

sentences.en: Did you like it? Did you not like it?
sentences.zh: 你喜欢它吗？还是不喜欢？
